sentences.text: Pluridens imelaki had a skull about 1.25 m long and a lower jaw with a nearly circular cross-section toward its tip.
The dentary – the main bone of the lower jaw – bore roughly 25 teeth.
Individuals could reach 5–6 m in length, and some specimens may have exceeded 9 m.
The jaws of certain specimens are robust and show injuries that hint at combat, perhaps over mates or territories.
The skull size of 1.25 m suggests a total body length of about 9 m or more.
Pluridens imelaki is exceptionally rare in Moroccan phosphates, known from only a single specimen among hundreds of mosasaur remains.
The type locality is Upper Couche III in Morocco.
Only one fossil occurrence has been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
Pluridens belongs to the family Mosasauridae.
Although once considered for a separate subfamily because of its high tooth count and distinctive tooth shape, it is now placed within the Halisaurinae.
Pluridens imelaki lived during the Late Cretaceous Maastrichtian age.
The Maastrichtian stage spans about 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
